newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Even without the support of businessman Eduardo Cojuangco, Vice President Joseph Estrada yesterday said he would still run for president. (INQUIRER)
- Following the acquittal of another accused drug trafficker, President Ramos ordered government agencies yesterday to wage total war against illegal drug syndicates. (STAR/BULLETIN)
- A South Korean security team has arrived in the Philippines to escort top North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop out of the country by special plane, Yonhap News agency said on Thursday. (INQUIRER)
- The decision of the Philippine Central Bank to suspend its maiden long-term Yankee bond offering has drawn mixed market reactions. (BUSINESS DAILY)

- The Securities and Exchange Commission and the Philippine Stock Exchange yesterday moved to investigate Empire East Land Holdings Inc, a unit of Megaworld Properties and Holdings Inc, for violation of insider trading and price manipulation. (MALAYA)
- The government must guard against increasing money supply growth that may trigger an inflation uptick and a "burning" trade gap, according to SBC Warburg director Jose Salceda. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
